page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Doing your homework
title: Doing your homework
topic: Language to use in customer research
description:
After Anna and Tom's dinner date, the idea for a new plastic vegetable is developing in Anna's mind. But before she can pitch the proposal to Paul she is going to need to do some thorough research!
This episode focuses on the language you need to carry out customer research.
phrases: Could I ask for your opinion on a new product we are hoping to develop?
What plastic products do you currently use?
What products would you like to see us sell in the future?
How do you feel about the idea of selling plastic vegetables?
Any particular vegetable you would like to see?

listening_challenge.question: What did the first company that Anna called sell?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello again. Last time on English at Work, we heard Anna leaving Tom crying into his cold pizza. He may not have had the evening he was expecting, but for Anna it was a huge success. She came up with an idea for a new plastic vegetable and now she needs to pitch it to Paul, the boss.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: … so I think I'll go for the blue, Marge, it matches my eyes… well almost…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Morning Denise!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh, hello Anna …yes, Anna, bright girl, what she sees in Tom I'll never know… what?!... ha, ha, I'm sure you would…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh hi Tom. You're in early.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Uh? Oh yeah, couldn't sleep after you'd left.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom, it was a fantastic night – unforgettable in fact. Thanks so much.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Did you hear that Marge? She said it was 'unforgettable'!  Looks like they're getting very serious…

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: You're such a gossip, Denise.  The only thing Anna is serious about is her new idea.  How's it going Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'm really excited about launching a new product, although Tom doesn't seem so keen.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Don't worry about him. You need to concentrate on convincing Paul that your new idea will bring in the business.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But how?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: You need to pitch the idea to him but before that, you need to do some research.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes, of course – research – but how do I do that?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Check out the competition, work out some costs and find out what new product people would really like to see. Why not do a customer survey?!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: A customer survey. Right. But what should I ask?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Say: 'Could I ask for your opinion on a new product we are hoping to develop?' 'What plastic products do you currently use?', 'What products would you like us to make in the future?', 'How do you feel about the idea of selling plastic vegetables?', 'Any particular vegetable you would like to see?'

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK, so it's like a questionnaire. I need to do some cold calling again!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Good luck!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I think I'm going to need some help with this. Tom, Denise, have you got time to help me… please?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Of course Anna.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, well it's a bit tricky with my… ouch… sprained arm. But go on. As it's you.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks. We need to call up some companies and find out how interested they would be in buying plastic vegetables.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh lovely. I love talking to people on the phone.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: You certainly do Denise!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Good Denise. If you work your way through our business directory, call our existing customers and ask these questions.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I'll get onto it straight away.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Great, and Tom, could you help me by cold calling some new businesses?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh yeah sure. I've got loads of contacts.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I suppose I had better make some calls too. Hmm, let's try this one. 7-4-3-9-1-0-0

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Hello. Plastic Purr-fection. Can I help you?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh hi. I'm Anna from Tip Top Trading, we make and sell plastic fruits. I'm trying some to get some opinions on a new product we're trying to develop. Can you spare a few minutes to help me?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Well I'm quite busy at the moment but I'll try and help.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thank you. I'll be as quick as I can.  Firstly, what plastic products do you use at the moment?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: All sorts – plastic balls, plastic fish, plastic mice…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Plastic mice?! Oh, I see. And… errr… what sort of things would you like us to sell… in the future?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Let's think… erm … more squeaky toys.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Squeaky toys?! What about plastic vegetables?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Do they squeak?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Err, not really. I think there might be some confusion here. Do you use plastic fruits in restaurants and shops?
Man
No. We just sell plastic toys… for cats, hence the name 'plastic purr-fection'.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh I see, ha, ha. A good name, but, I'm sorry you're not really the business I was looking for. Thanks for your time anyway. Bye.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Bye. Get down Tiddles!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Uh-oh Anna. It's a good idea to check exactly what type of business you are calling before carrying out your survey. Better luck next time!  If you're doing some research and want to get the opinions of your customers, here's a reminder of the questions you could ask:
Could I ask for your opinion on a new product we are hoping to develop?
What plastic products do you currently use?
What products would you like to see us sell in the future?
How do you feel about the idea of selling plastic vegetables?
Any particular vegetable you would like to see?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Let's find out how the team is getting on.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: That was fun. I called 10 companies, asked them your questions – one man asked me out for dinner – anyway, I've created a database and put all the information there.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Well I've called 20 companies and they all say plastic vegetables would be a great addition to their range… especially aubergines!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Great. Well, I had some success too so I'll put all the results in that database.  Thanks everyone. Oh no… what's happened?  Denise! Denise! Everything's disappeared off the computer!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Hey, my computer's gone blank. We've lost all our documents!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh no a computer crash! Has Tip Top Trading lost all its valuable information? Find out next time in English at Work. Bye!
